players.product: US utility - UHV transformer buyer (Hyosung HICO end customer)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: near-term milestones. The final wind turbine was installed last week on the offshore wind project Eversource exited ('65 out of 65 turbines are installed'), and the constructing partner Ørsted 'has stated that we will be COD by the end of the year'. FERC must set the new transmission rate under Eversource's Section 205 filing by November 30, effective in billing December 1. In the Connecticut Light and Power rate case, hearings start in February with a draft decision in May.
quarterly_data.figure: 65 out of 65 turbines installed, COD by end of year; FERC new rate by November 30 (billing December 1); CL&P hearings February, draft decision May

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the FERC transmission ROE: the new rate is 'going to be a lot better than 9.57%'; Eversource took FERC's formula, applied it and 'came out with this rate of 11.37%' (as stated in the talk). He calls the FERC order 'significantly flawed' because the 2014 order underlying the first part of the test was vacated; Eversource agrees to a 15-month refund but disputes any longer retroactive refund. The court told FERC to certify the record within 30 days, and he thinks a final court decision could come 'as soon as August' ('August the 27th'). Eversource is 'ready to sit down at any time' to work it through.
quarterly_data.figure: filed ROE 11.37% vs current 9.57%; 15-month refund accepted; court decision possibly in August

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: in Connecticut Eversource was owed over $1 billion in storm costs and 'achieved 96% of our ask' - $960 million in storm costs - with an opportunity to get the remaining $40 million; the securitization plan was filed last Friday. Carrying charges it asked for are 'not over yet', and 'we're getting carrying charges right now until such time as the securitization happens'. About $500 million of New Hampshire storm costs should come 'probably within about a year'. 'This is over $1 billion in cash coming in the door.'
quarterly_data.figure: Connecticut storm costs $960 million recovered (96% of ask), $40 million still sought; New Hampshire about $500 million within about a year

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the new five-member Connecticut commission (PURA): it took a Yankee Gas draft decision of $70 million to $104 million with a 9.47% ROE ('the highest ROE in Connecticut'); it gave $200 million to prefund the storm fund; about $125 million of public benefit charges is now being bonded ('They sent us a check for $125 million'). Eversource had 'shut the faucet off in Connecticut' on investment until it got the storm costs.
quarterly_data.figure: Yankee Gas $104 million vs $70 million draft, ROE 9.47%; $200 million storm fund prefunding; $125 million public benefit charges bonded

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: 'we just won last week a project with Iberdrola to build a line up to Canada', in the regulated space: the line is $2.2 billion, '$700 million of that is ours', and it 'will be added to the plan' (the five-year capital plan of $26.5 billion). Connecticut AMI is 'a billion-dollar opportunity, not in the plan' - a five-year program for which Eversource seeks a tracker, starting with a new billing system; it 'was only going to cost probably $750 million to $800 million' but because of delays 'now the cost is going to be $1 billion'.
quarterly_data.figure: $700 million share of a $2.2 billion transmission line to be added to the $26.5 billion plan; Connecticut AMI $1 billion (was $750 million to $800 million), not in plan

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: 'we are seeing extraordinary electric growth in our region' from electrification. Three substations are getting filed right now in Massachusetts; the Cambridge substation (120 feet underground, $1.8 billion) is in the plan, while new ones in Boston and the suburbs are not. Eversource keeps '900 megawatts of solar that we can build in Massachusetts' in its back pocket. ISO New England is coming to Eversource to unlock generation with projects 'running 30, 50, $70 million' (mostly onshore solar and wind) and probably has four or five now, after the $100 million Boston Reliability Project that 'we brought in ahead of schedule and under budget'. A $100 million Dartmouth College DREAM project received a federal grant for 50 of the 100 million, announced the day before the talk.
quarterly_data.figure: Cambridge substation $1.8 billion, 120 feet underground; 900 megawatts of solar optionality; ISO New England projects 30, 50, $70 million; DREAM project $100 million with 50 million federal grant

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on data centers and regional supply: 'I am anti-data centers. I don't like data centers... We're not interested in a data center.' His reasons: 'We have a finite amount of generation in the region', electrification gives enough growth without the volatility, and he prefers employers of '2, 3, 400 people'. He contrasts ISO New England's lack of volatility with PJM, says offshore wind 'at a 50% availability factor is a game changer for us' in winter months, and expects the Enbridge gas line to let the region get off LNG. The Millstone contract is up in 2029, and he expects the Connecticut rate decision before any Millstone decision.
quarterly_data.figure: no data-center load sought; offshore wind 50% availability factor; Millstone contract up in 2029
